resources.string: If going back does not close it, you go to the home screen.
Enter your current PIN to change it.
Without a PIN it will be easier to skip your own rules.
A shorter wait gives you less time to think it over.
Pattern on. It is asked for in apps that have it in their rule.
Accessibility is off: nothing is blocked.
What Pausa asks for and why
Everything stays on this phone: your rules, the use of the apps you control (30 days) and your settings. No account, no internet.
Draw your current pattern to change it.
Draw your current pattern. Apps that ask for it will stop asking.
Your rules, usage, statistics, exceptions and PIN are deleted. This cannot be undone.
Last confirmation: Pausa will go back to how it was when first installed.
%1$d to %2$d digits. It is not a bank password: it is there to stop an impulse.
The two PINs do not match.
A focus session or a strict block is in progress. You will be able to delete everything when it ends.
Apps you turn on here get past every block and focus session. Better to keep few.
No block or focus session will affect it.
A focus session or a strict block is in progress. Exceptions can be added when it ends.

It is the only thing Pausa needs. It lets Pausa know which app is on screen so it can show you a pause or a block, and recognise the sections you choose to block (like Shorts). You turn it on yourself, by hand, in Android settings, and you can turn it off whenever you want.
It does not read your messages, photos or passwords. It does not store what you see. It only notes the names of the apps you control and how long you use them, to apply your limits.
Internet, contacts, location, camera, microphone or storage. Without the internet permission, Pausa cannot send anything out of the phone: Android guarantees it, it is not just a promise.
If the switch is grayed out

Android blocks the service of apps installed from outside the store until you allow it: open the app info, tap ⋮ (top right) and choose “Allow restricted settings”. Then go back to accessibility settings.
To keep it from turning off by itself (Samsung)

If Pausa stops working with the screen off, go to Settings → Battery → Background usage limits, remove it from “Sleeping apps” and add it to “Never sleeping apps”. Names may vary a bit depending on the One UI version.
